messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 - /auth/validate spike: JWT signature invalid rate increased across prod (US-EAST, EU-WEST). Incident ID: PD-98321. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-98321 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Incident PD-98321 triggered (P1). Notifying on-call.

alice: acked. I'm looking. Seeing ~12% 401s from verifier in the last 2m on service auth-verifier.

alice: quick snapshot: 5xx from verifier: 0.2%, 401/invalid-signature: 12%, latencies within normal. Graphs: https://grafana.example/d/abcd/auth-validate

maria: I pulled a few failing JWTs — kid header present, jwk lookup to our JWKS returns keys that don't match the signature. We rotated keys 3m ago in the key-service deploy.

raj: Oncall here. If this is a key mismatch from rotation we should either rollback key rotation or add fallback to accept old key. Which is less customer-impacting?

alice: I'm starting a rollback of the key rotation commit (git sha: a1b2c3d). Rolling back key-service to pre-rotation.

deploy-bot: Rollback started for service:key-service by alice. Triggering canary rollback.
deploy-bot: Rollback complete for service:key-service. All canaries passed.

alice: Post-rollback - error rate dropped from 12% -> 4% within 90s. Still seeing residual 401s for tokens minted during the 3m rotation window.

maria: Confirmed. Tokens minted between 1812345600 and 1812345780 used the new signing key. Those tokens will fail unless verifier accepts both keys or we reissue.

zach: Support impact: Top affected customers (estimated failed auth calls): Acme Inc (~2.3k requests, ~30m impact), FinCo (~1.1k, ~20m), EduCorp (~420, ~5m). I'm drafting customer message and setting priority.

alice: I can hotpatch verifier to accept both key ids for 12h: allow_kid_aliases + JWKS cache rehydrate. Minimal downtime and no forced reissue. Pushing patch to auth-verifier.

alice: patch diff:
```
# hotpatch config snippet
auth.verifier.allow_kid_aliases: true
auth.jwks.cache_ttl_seconds: 300
auth.jwks.prior_keys_accept_window: 86400  # accept previous key for 24h
```

alice: Applied hotpatch on prod; reloaded verifier config. Watching metrics.

maria: After patch, 401s reduced to ~0.4% and trending to zero. Good signal. We should avoid immediate token revocation; will create a follow-up to rotate keys with a canary smoke test that validates issued tokens.

support-bot: Notifying CS and creating status page draft. Customers notified: initial advisory to affected accounts.

raj: Setting incident state -> mitigated. Escalating to Eng Manager for RCA and postmortem: incorrect key mapping in the rotation job (rotation automation used a different kid prefix than verifier expected).

alice: Handing off monitoring and postmortem to maria (next on-call). My shift ends in 30m. I'll add runbook steps I ran to the incident doc: rollback, hotpatch, accept-window config, customer outreach.

maria: Taking over. Will own postmortem and follow-ups: add canary validation for key rotation, add smoke tests that mint/test tokens, add alert for >1% invalid-signature over 5m.

zach: CS will send follow-up update in 1h with timeline and remediation steps.

incident-bot: PD-98321 updated: status=mitigated, assigned_to=maria, notes="Rollback + hotpatch fallback applied; residual tokens handled by accept-window."

alice: Closing the paging loop here. If anyone sees a regression ping me or reopen the PD. :thumbsup:

maria: Will run RCA and schedule postmortem. Thanks all for the quick response.

support-bot: Post-incident actions created: #1 - add canary + smoke to key rotation; #2 - increase JWKS cache visibility; #3 - update runbook.

raj: Agreed. Follow-up owner list: maria (RCA), alice (runbook updates), zach (customer comms), eng-sre (automation fix).

incident-bot: Incident PD-98321 resolved state: mitigated -> monitoring. Closing Slack thread.
